common_name: Cool Igloo Chrysanthemum (Hardy Raspberry Cushion Mum)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring or fall; Cool Igloo is part of the patented Igloo series of dwarf, naturally mounding garden mums bred for uniform habit and garden hardiness.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile soil; Cool Igloo grows into a dense, low, uniformly rounded cushion without pinching. Masses of raspberry-purple double flowers up to 2 inches wide cover the mound in a heavy late-summer into fall display. As part of the Igloo series bred for dependable first-year flowering and garden hardiness, it holds its compact mounded shape through the season and is well suited to the front of the border or mixed containers. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring to maintain vigor.

common_name: Morden Cameo Chrysanthemum (Cold-Hardy Canadian Prairie Mum, Creamy White)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring so roots establish well before winter; Morden Cameo was bred at the Morden Research Station in Manitoba for exceptional prairie winter hardiness and early autumn bloom in short-season climates.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile soil; Morden Cameo grows into an upright, spreading clump of grayish-green, fragrant ferny foliage. Fully double, creamy white daisy flowers with buttery yellow overtones cover the plant from late August through October, blooming early enough to color up reliably even in short prairie seasons. Its Agriculture Canada breeding gives it outstanding winter hardiness to Zone 3 without winter mulch. Flowers are excellent for cutting; cut plants back in early spring before new growth resumes, and lift and divide overgrown clumps every two to three years.
